info.title: HtAG Analytics API
info.description:
Unified API specification for HtAG Analytics — Australia's property intelligence platform.

This specification covers the **External** (paid developer) surface of the HtAG Analytics API, organised by tag groups.

## Authentication

All endpoints require an API key issued via the HtAG Developer Portal, sent in the `x-api-key` request header. See the security scheme below.

## Billing & Usage Tracking

Every successful (`2xx`) response to a billable endpoint carries telemetry headers describing the cost and unit count of that request. Read them directly from the response to drive per-call charge-back, usage dashboards, or balance monitoring — no separate API call required.

| Header | Example | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `X-Billing-Cost` | `0.136` | Amount charged for this request, in AUD. |
| `X-Billing-Balance` | `49.864` | Account balance (AUD) after this deduction. |
| `X-Billing-Units` | `4` | Number of billable units counted (rows, addresses, or properties — endpoint-dependent). |
| `X-Billing-Tier` | `tier1` | Pricing tier applied: `free`, `tier1`, `tier2`, or `tier3`. |
| `X-Billing-Free-Remaining` | `21` | Free-tier units remaining on the account. Absent when no free allowance applies. |
| `X-Billing-Free-Granted` | `1` | Free-tier units consumed by this request. Absent when no free allowance applies. |

Notes:

- Non-`2xx` responses (4xx / 5xx) are not charged and do not carry these
  headers.

- Browser clients (`fetch`, `XHR`) can read these headers via the
  `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` policy already configured on the API.

- `X-Billing-Cost` is a decimal string in AUD — there is no separate
  "credit" currency; the account balance is denominated in AUD.


## Attribution Notices

- **ABS / SEIFA Data**: Certain endpoints return indicators derived from the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS),
  including SEIFA indices (IRSD, IRSAD, IER, IEO) and Census-derived metrics (public housing rates, private rental rates).
  This data is sourced from the ABS and licensed under the
  [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) licence.
  Users of this API must include the following attribution in any product or publication that incorporates this data:
  **"Incorporates data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics, © Commonwealth of Australia, licensed under CC BY 4.0."**

- **GNAF**: Address data incorporates or is derived from the Geocoded National Address File (G-NAF)
  © Geoscape Australia, licensed under the [End User Licence Agreement (EULA)](https://geoscape.com.au/legal/data-copyright-and-disclaimer/).

tags.name: Address Environment

tags.name: Address Demographics

Returns ABS SEIFA indices and Census-derived housing tenure metrics.

tags.name: Address Schools
tags.description:
Nearby school data for Australian addresses.
Returns government schools (catchment zone match), Catholic and Independent schools (radius search),
with ACARA rankings and My School identifiers.

tags.name: Address Standardisation
tags.description: Batch standardisation of free-text Australian addresses into canonical components and address keys.

tags.name: Address Features
tags.description:
Per-address environment, transport, lifestyle, hazard, safety, and aviation proximity indicators derived from OpenStreetMap data.

Each endpoint exposes one strict thematic slice; clients compose multi-theme views by calling multiple endpoints with the same `address_keys` list.

Bulk-only lookup by `address_keys` (CSV, up to 50). Unknown keys are omitted from `results` — clients detect misses by comparing input length to `total`.

tags.name: Property
tags.description:
Property-level intelligence including physical attributes, price and rent estimates,
and sold property radius search.

tags.name: Market Summary
tags.description: Core market headline metrics — typical price, rent, yield, sales/rental volumes, estimated dwellings, and population.

tags.name: Market Commentary
tags.description: AI-generated narrative market commentary for suburbs and LGAs.

tags.name: Market Growth
tags.description: Multi-horizon cumulative and annualised growth rates for prices, rents, and yields.

tags.name: Market Supply
tags.description:
Supply-side metrics including lot size, inventory, building approvals, and hold periods.
Includes current snapshots, long-term trends, and short-term trends via slope analysis.

tags.name: Market Demand
tags.description:
Demand-side metrics including days on market, discounting, vacancy, clearance rate, and search interest.
Includes current snapshots, long-term trends, and short-term trends via slope analysis.

tags.name: Market Scores
tags.description: Relative Composite Score (RCS™) rankings, HAPI score, volatility index, and confidence levels.

tags.name: Market Fundamentals
tags.description: Socio-economic fundamentals including IRSAD, ownership/housing ratios, and affordability index (years to own).

tags.name: Market Cycle
tags.description:
Growth rate cycle position, GRC index, growth projection decomposition (GPD), growth stability profile (GSP),
and forward-looking projected annual returns.

tags.name: Market Risk
tags.description: Environmental risk indices (flood, bushfire) and economic diversity measures for an area.

tags.name: Market Query
tags.description:
Query suburb or LGA market snapshots using a flexible public filter DSL.
Accepts nested and/or/not logic plus eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte/in/nin/like/ilike operators across public metric names. Response is allow-listed to a compact set of headline fields.

tags.name: Market Rank
tags.description:
Shortlist ranking: weighted decile scoring of a caller-supplied list of area_ids across configurable numeric metrics. Returns score and dense sequential rank per area_id, plus methodology diagnostics. Premium tier.
Scores are relative to the supplied shortlist — the same area in two different shortlists yields two different scores.

tags.name: Market Trends
tags.description: Market Trends domain: historical price, rent, yield, growth, demand profile, and monthly building approval trends.

tags.name: Supply-Demand Trends
tags.description:
Detailed supply-demand trend endpoints (Restricted pricing tier, rate-limited to **10,000 billable rows per calendar month per API key** per endpoint; see each operation's `x-htg-rate-limit` extension).
Includes stock-on-market, inventory, days on market, clearance rate, vacancy, hold period, and search index trends.

tags.name: Demographics
tags.description:
Suburb-level demographic and enrichment data derived from ABS Census 2021, CABEE business counts, and healthcare cluster pipelines.
All demographics endpoints are billed at the Standard tier ($0.034/row).

tags.name: Spatial H3 — Price & Rent
tags.description:
H3-indexed median price, rent, gross yield, and years-to-own surfaces at resolutions 5–9.
All metric endpoints accept geographic filters (loc_pid, lga_pid, sa2_code, sa3_code, sa4_code, gcc_name) and property_type/beds/baths slicing.

tags.name: Spatial H3 — Market
tags.description: H3-indexed market activity surfaces: days on market, days on rental market (DORM), lot size, inventory months, holding return, vacancy, hold period, and listed price.

tags.name: Spatial H3 — Socio-Environmental
tags.description: H3-indexed socio-economic and environmental overlays: IRSD, IRSAD, IER, IEO deprivation indices, economic diversity, and flood/bushfire exposure percentages.

tags.name: Spatial H3 — Reference
tags.description: H3 grid reference utilities: available resolutions, cell geometry (boundary/center), hierarchical navigation (parent/children), and neighbour discovery.

tags.name: Reference
tags.description:
Free reference data lookups for Australian localities (suburbs), LGAs (Local Government Areas), and address-key enumeration within a single geography.
Use these endpoints to resolve area_id values used across all market endpoints, or to list address keys belonging to a specific SA1, SA2, locality, or LGA.
Reference endpoints are quota-limited per endpoint — see each operation's `x-htg-rate-limit` for the applicable monthly quota.

tags.name: Concordance
tags.description:
Geographic concordance and translation between ABS statistical geographies (SA2, SAL, LGA code, postcode) and HTAG identifiers (loc_pid, lga_pid). Billed at the Reference tier ($0.001/row).

## SA2 ↔ SAL (Locality) Area Mapping

ABS Statistical Area Level 2 (SA2) and Suburb/Locality (SAL) are two independent geographic classifications that **do not align**. A single SA2 can contain many localities, and a locality can span multiple SA2s. The `abs_sa2_sal_map` table provides area-based multipliers to convert metric values between these two geographies.

### Multipliers

| Field | Formula | Plain English |
|-------|---------|---------------|
| `area_perc_sal` | `SAL_area / SA2_area` | How big the locality is relative to the SA2 |
| `area_perc_sa2` | `SA2_area / SAL_area` | How big the SA2 is relative to the locality |

These are reciprocals: `area_perc_sa2 = 1 / area_perc_sal`.

### Converting SA2 → localities (distributing data down)

Use `area_perc_sal` as the multiplier. Each locality receives its proportional share of the SA2-level value.

```
locality_value = SA2_value × area_perc_sal
```

**Example:** If SA2 Braidwood (3,418 km², spanning 38 localities) has 100 building approvals, BRAIDWOOD locality (`area_perc_sal = 0.0686`) receives `100 × 0.0686 = 6.9` approvals.

### Converting localities → SA2 (aggregating data up)

For rate/price metrics, weight each locality's contribution by its area share:

```
SA2_value = Σ (locality_value_i × area_perc_sal_i) / Σ (area_perc_sal_i)
```

For counts (e.g. sales volume), simply sum the locality-level values.

### Simple vs complex mappings

- **1:1** — Lyneham, ACT: `area_perc_sal ≈ 0.99`, effectively a pass-through.
- **1:many** — Braidwood SA2: 38 localities, each a small fraction (`area_perc_sal` 0.7%–7.8%). The `area_perc_sal` values sum to ~1.0.

### Filtering & assumptions

Intersection slivers where overlap < 5% of the locality's area are excluded. This is an **area-weighted proportional allocation** — it assumes uniform distribution. Works well for aggregate counts and volumes; less accurate for rate/price metrics in areas with uneven density.

Source: geometric intersection of ABS SA2 (2021 edition) and SAL shapefiles.

get.summary: Resolve address identity and coordinates
get.description:
Returns the canonical address key, GNAF identifiers, coordinates, ABS geography codes,
mesh block classification, and standardised address elements for the requested address.

Query by free-text `address`. Optionally filter by `mb_category_2021`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum candidate matches to return. Omitted, the service default applies.

200.description: Address geocode records matching the query

get.summary: Retrieve environmental risk overlays for an address
get.description:
Returns flood, bushfire, heritage, and zoning indicators for the requested address(es).

**Exactly one** of the following query parameters must be supplied:
- `address` (free-text lookup)
- `address_keys` (batch by canonical keys)
- `legal_parcel_id` (by legal parcel)

200.description: Environmental overlay records matching the query

get.summary: Retrieve socio-economic and demographic indicators for an address
get.description:
Returns ABS SEIFA indices and Census-derived housing tenure metrics for the requested address(es).

## Attribution Requirement

Data returned by this endpoint is derived from the **Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS)**
and is licensed under the
[Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) licence.

**API consumers MUST include the following attribution** in any product, report, or publication
that incorporates data from this endpoint:

> *"Incorporates data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics, © Commonwealth of Australia, licensed under CC BY 4.0."*

### SEIFA Index Descriptions

| Field  | Index Name                                          | Description |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| IRSD   | Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage       | Summarises economic and social disadvantage (income, education, employment, housing). Lower decile = greater disadvantage. |
| IRSAD  | Index of Relative Socio-economic Advantage and Disadvantage | Summarises both advantage and disadvantage. Lower decile = greater disadvantage; higher = greater advantage. |
| IER    | Index of Economic Resources                         | Reflects financial aspects (income, housing costs, assets). |
| IEO    | Index of Education and Occupation                   | Reflects education and occupation characteristics. |

All SEIFA fields are expressed as **decile ranks (1–10)** relative to the national distribution.

**Exactly one** of the following query parameters must be supplied:
- `address` (free-text lookup)
- `address_keys` (batch by canonical keys)
- `legal_parcel_id` (by legal parcel)

200.description: Demographic indicator records matching the query

get.summary: Retrieve schools relevant to an address
get.description:
Returns schools relevant to an Australian address.

**Government (public) schools** are returned only if the address falls within the school’s official catchment zone (point-in-polygon match).

**Catholic and Independent schools** are returned if they are within the specified search radius (default 5 km, max 50 km).

Each school record includes the ACARA SML ID (for [My School](https://www.myschool.edu.au)), school name, sector, type, location, ACARA percentile ranking (where available), distance, and catchment flag.

**Exactly one** of `address` or `address_key` must be supplied.

parameters.name: radius_m
parameters.description: Search radius in metres for Catholic and Independent schools. Does not affect Government schools (catchment zones). Default 5000, max 50000.

post.summary: Batch standardise Australian addresses and generate address keys
post.description:
Accepts up to 50 single-line (free text) Australian addresses, standardises each into
its component elements, and generates a canonical address key.
Only Australian addresses are supported.

**Ordering guarantee:** results are returned in the same order as the request's `addresses[]` array, and each result carries an `input_index` field pointing back to its position in the request. Clients should pair results with inputs by `input_index` rather than by positional or string matching.

get.summary: Retrieve walkability score and urban-tier classification for an address
get.description:
Composite walkability score (0–10) and urban-tier classification for the requested address(es).

**Note.** Roughly 10.6% of national addresses have `walkability_score = 0`. These are real zeros (remote / no POIs in radius), not nulls — do not filter them out as "missing data".

get.summary: Retrieve public-transit, active-transport, and EV refuelling proximity for an address
get.description:
Distance metrics for rail, bus, tram, and ferry infrastructure plus the nearest EV charging station.

**Note.** `nearest_tram_stop_m` returns the sentinel value `200000` (never null) when no tram network covers the address — only Melbourne, Adelaide, parts of Sydney light rail, and the Gold Coast have tram networks. Every `nearest_*_m` field follows the same convention: numeric in every row, with `200000` indicating "no qualifying feature within the search horizon".

200.description: Transport proximity records matching the query

get.summary: Retrieve CBD, airport, and major-road proximity for an address
get.description:
Long-distance travel context: distance to nearest CBD/GPO, airport, and major-road network.

**Note.** `cbd_distance_m` measures distance to the nearest CBD/GPO Australia-wide — not to the capital city of the address's state.

Airport here is "distance to terminal as travel hub". Aviation noise / overflight signals (flight path + runway axis) are exposed via `/address/aviation`.

get.summary: Retrieve coastal / water-adjacent feature proximity for an address
get.description:
Beach, coastline, water-body, surf club, and marina proximity.

`nearest_ferry_terminal_m` is intentionally exposed via `/address/transport` (transit theme), not here.

get.summary: Retrieve park, dog-park, and recreation proximity for an address
get.description: Park, dog-park, and recreation-area proximity and density.

200.description: Green-space proximity records matching the query

get.summary: Retrieve discretionary lifestyle amenities for an address
get.description:
Dining, drinking, fitness, golf, and cultural amenities — cafés, restaurants, pubs, fitness specialty venues, golf courses, museum / galleries.

Day-to-day essentials (supermarkets, healthcare, childcare, libraries, community centres) are exposed separately via `/address/essentials`.

get.summary: Retrieve day-to-day essentials and community services proximity for an address
get.description: Day-to-day necessities: groceries (supermarket, shopping centre, food retail), healthcare (hospital, medical clinic, pharmacy), childcare, university, plus community services (community centre, library).

200.description: Essentials proximity records matching the query

get.summary: Retrieve hazard-adjacent landmark proximity for an address
get.description:
Proximity to natural-hazard and culturally-undesirable landmarks: nearest bushfire-prone vegetation, landfill, cemetery.

**Companion to `/address/environment`.** This endpoint returns the proximity-based view ("how close is the risk landscape?"). `/address/environment` returns the authoritative jurisdiction-flagged view (Y/N for flood, bushfire, heritage). Use both together for a complete risk picture.

get.summary: Retrieve industrial sites and electrical infrastructure adjacency for an address
get.description:
Negative-signal due-diligence bundle: proximity to industrial sites and electrical infrastructure (power lines, substations).

Road and airport nuisance signals are exposed via `/address/cbd-proximity` (the distance fields there double as nuisance signals — `2 km from nearest major road` = well-connected; `40 m from nearest major road` = noise-affected). Flight-path noise is on `/address/aviation`. No duplication across endpoints.

get.summary: Retrieve emergency-services proximity for an address
get.description: Distance to nearest fire station and police station, plus a 500 m police-presence boolean.

200.description: Safety-services proximity records matching the query

get.summary: Retrieve aviation flight-path and runway adjacency for an address
get.description:
Flight-path overhead and runway adjacency signals. Differs from `/address/cbd-proximity` `nearest_commercial_airport_m` (which represents the scheduled-commercial terminal as a travel hub) — this endpoint captures aviation noise / overflight rather than airport access. The runway layer covers all aerodromes (including general aviation), so `nearest_runway_m` may be far smaller than `nearest_commercial_airport_m` for the same address.

**Note.** `under_flight_path` is corridor membership — true iff the address sits within a runway's extended-centreline approach/ departure corridor (beyond the runway end) AND ≤ 1000 m laterally from that centreline. `nearest_runway_axis_distance_m` is the lateral distance from that centreline.

get.summary: Retrieve local road-infrastructure features for an address
get.description:
Local road-geometry features. Currently roundabouts only — distance to the nearest roundabout plus 50 m / 100 m presence booleans.

Long-distance road connectivity (major roads, CBD, airport) is on `/address/cbd-proximity`.

200.description: Road-infrastructure proximity records matching the query

get.summary: Retrieve physical property attributes for an address
get.description:
Returns the physical characteristics of the property at the specified address key,
including property type, bedrooms, bathrooms, parking, land area, floor area,
and build/renovation date.

get.summary: Retrieve valuation estimates and transaction history for an address
get.description:
Returns index-adjusted CMA (comparative market analysis) estimates for sale price and rent.
Index-adjusted CMA: estimates produced by adjusting historical sale/rental prices by market index
(typical price) changes since the last transaction date. Also returns the most recent sale and rental
transaction records for the specified address key.

parameters.name: cma_method
parameters.description: CMA methodology to use for estimates. Currently only Index-Adjusted (IA) is available.

get.summary: Retrieve market position indicators for an address
get.description:
Returns property-level market position metrics for the specified address key,
including rental proportion, years to own, and typical hold period.

get.summary: Retrieve the full sale and rental history for an address
get.description: Returns every recorded sale and/or rental transaction for the specified address key, ordered most-recent first within each array. Use `sold` and `rented` to choose which histories to return; by default both are returned. At least one of `sold` or `rented` must be true. Sale prices are whole AUD and rent values are weekly AUD/week. `property_type` is reported once at the top level as the canonical dwelling type of the most recent requested transaction; same-date ties prefer sale.

parameters.name: sold
parameters.description: Include sale history (default true).

parameters.name: rented
parameters.description: Include rental history (default true).

get.summary: Search for sold properties within a radius of an address or coordinates
get.description:
Radius-based search of sold properties using an address key, free-text address, or lat/lon point.

At least **one** of `address`, `address_key`, or both `lat` and `lon` must be provided.

Supports filters for radius, proximity, property type, price, dates, and features.

**Proximity and radius.** `radius` applies only when `proximity` is `any` (the default). Both named modes ignore it: `sameSuburb` returns the whole suburb and `sameStreet` returns the whole street, however far from the anchor. For example `GET /property/sold/search?address_key=...&radius=500&proximity=sameSuburb` returns matching sales from across that suburb — the 500 m is discarded, not applied — and `proximity=sameStreet` likewise covers the entire street, while the same request with `proximity=any` returns only sales within 500 m of the anchor. Both named modes need an `address` or `address_key`. See the `proximity` parameter for the per-value rules.

**Pagination.** Results are ordered by `sale_date` descending with `address_key` as a unique tie-breaker, then `offset` rows are skipped and up to `limit` rows returned. Omit both parameters to get `limit=100&offset=0` — for example `GET /property/sold/search?address_key=...` returns rows 1-100, and `GET /property/sold/search?address_key=...&limit=25&offset=50` returns rows 51-75. Advance `offset` by `limit` for the next page and stop when `total` is less than `limit`. An `offset` at or beyond the end returns `200` with an empty `results` array and `total: 0`.

**Billing.** `total` is the number of rows in *this page* — not the count of all matching records — and is the billable row count. Rows skipped by `offset` are never returned and never charged.

**Filter naming.** Every filter below is accepted under two spellings: the camelCase name and its snake_case twin (`saleValueMin` / `sale_value_min`, `startDate` / `start_date`, `propertyType` / `property_type`, and so on). Supply either. If you supply both, the **camelCase value wins** and the snake_case value is discarded silently — so do not send both with different values. An explicit `false` or `0` counts as a supplied value; only omitting a parameter falls through to its twin.

**Date window.** `startDate` / `endDate` bound the sale date inclusively. Omitting `startDate` applies a default window of 90 days before the effective `endDate`. That is a default, not a maximum lookback: an explicit `startDate` a year back is honoured in full.

**Price bounds and unknown prices.** `saleValueMin` / `saleValueMax` are inclusive. `includeSaleValueUnknown` governs rows whose sale price is unknown and applies only when no price bound is set: a price bound always excludes unknown prices, because an unknown price cannot be compared against a bound. Setting the flag `false` always excludes them.

**Unrecognised parameters are rejected.** A query parameter this operation does not implement returns `400` with `error: "unknown_query_parameters"`, naming the offending parameters and — where one exists — the canonical parameter that replaces them. Nothing is queried and nothing is billed. Ignoring such a name, which is what happened before, turned a filtered-looking request into a billed, silently unfiltered result. `saleFromDate` and `saleToDate` were declared here until this change and are now rejected; use `startDate` / `endDate`. A misspelling is never matched to a nearby parameter — the response lists `accepted_parameters` instead, so you can correct it yourself.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description:
Query by a freeform address.
**Only one of `address`, `address_key`, `lon`, or `lat` can be provided in a single request.**

parameters.name: proximity
parameters.description:
Spatial relation between the search anchor and the rows returned (default: `any`). Values are case-sensitive.

- `any` — return sales within `radius` of the anchor.

- `sameStreet` — **`radius` is ignored.** Returns matching sales from anywhere on the anchor's street, however far from the anchor, with the other filters and `limit`/`offset` applying as usual. The street is matched on its canonical name, type and suffix within the anchor's suburb, so a same-named street in another suburb, a different street type (`King Street` vs `King Avenue`) and a longer name (`Main` vs `Main Ridge`) are all excluded. A sale whose address is not present in HtAG's address reference data cannot be confirmed to be on the street and is not returned. Sales with no coordinates are included. Requires `address` or `address_key` — a `lat`/`lon`-only anchor has no street to match and is rejected with `400`.

- `sameSuburb` — **`radius` is ignored.** Returns matching sales from anywhere in the anchor's suburb, however far from the anchor, with the other filters and `limit`/`offset` applying as usual. Sales with no coordinates are included. Requires `address` or `address_key` — a `lat`/`lon`-only anchor is rejected with `400`.

`radius` is still range-checked when it is ignored, so `radius=6000&proximity=sameSuburb` (or `sameStreet`) is rejected as out of range before the search runs.

parameters.name: propertyType
parameters.description: Filter by **canonical property type**. Accepts a comma-separated list or repeated query parameters (e.g. `propertyType=house,semi-detached` or `propertyType=house&propertyType=semi-detached`). Each canonical value expands server-side to the raw `property_type` rows it represents — for example `semi-detached` covers townhouses, villas, duplexes and terraces; `unit` covers units, apartments, flats and studios. Allowed canonical values: `house`, `unit`, `semi-detached`, `land`, `lifestyle-retirement`, `rural`, `other`. Omit to return all property types.

parameters.name: saleValueMin
parameters.description: Minimum sale value (AUD)

parameters.name: saleValueMax
parameters.description: Maximum sale value (AUD)

parameters.name: includeSaleValueUnknown
parameters.description: Include properties where sale value is unknown (default true)

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Include properties sold on or after this date (ISO 8601). Omitted, it defaults to 90 days before the effective `endDate`. That is a default, not a maximum lookback — an explicit earlier `startDate` is honoured in full.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: Include properties sold on or before this date (ISO 8601). Defaults to today.

parameters.name: bedroomsMin
parameters.description: Minimum number of bedrooms

parameters.name: bedroomsMax
parameters.description: Maximum number of bedrooms

parameters.name: bathroomsMin
parameters.description: Minimum number of bathrooms

parameters.name: bathroomsMax
parameters.description: Maximum number of bathrooms

parameters.name: carSpacesMin
parameters.description: Minimum number of car spaces

parameters.name: carSpacesMax
parameters.description: Maximum number of car spaces

parameters.name: landAreaMin
parameters.description: Minimum land area in square metres

parameters.name: landAreaMax
parameters.description: Maximum land area in square metres

parameters.name: includeSameSuburbNoLatLon
parameters.description: For `address_key` queries, also include same-suburb properties that have no coordinates (default false).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return in one page. Defaults to 100 when omitted; must be an integer between 1 and 1000.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of matching **rows** to skip before `limit` is applied. Defaults to 0 when omitted; must be an integer >= 0. This is a row offset, not a page number — `limit=25&offset=50` returns rows 51-75.

200.description: One page of sold property records. `total` is the number of rows in this page (also the billable row count), not the count of all matching records.

get.summary: Search for rented properties within a radius of an address or coordinates
get.description:
Radius-based search of rental listings using an address key, free-text address, or lat/lon point.

At least **one** of `address`, `address_key`, or both `lat` and `lon` must be provided.

Supports filters for radius, proximity, property type, advertised rent, listing dates, and basic features.

**Proximity and radius.** `radius` applies only when `proximity` is `any` (the default). Both named modes ignore it: `sameSuburb` returns the whole suburb and `sameStreet` the whole street, however far from the anchor. For example `GET /property/rented/search?address_key=...&radius=500&proximity=sameSuburb` returns matching listings from across that suburb — the 500 m is discarded, not applied — so `distance_km` on the returned rows can exceed `radius` under either named mode. Both named modes need an `address` or `address_key`. See the `proximity` parameter for the per-value rules.

**Pagination.** Results are ordered by `list_date` descending with `address_key` as a tie-breaker, then `offset` rows are skipped and up to `limit` rows returned. Omit both parameters to get `limit=100&offset=0` — for example `GET /property/rented/search?address_key=...` returns rows 1-100, and `GET /property/rented/search?address_key=...&limit=25&offset=50` returns rows 51-75. Advance `offset` by `limit` for the next page and stop when `total` is less than `limit`. An `offset` at or beyond the end returns `200` with an empty `results` array and `total: 0`.

**Billing.** `total` is the number of rows in *this page* — not the count of all matching records — and is the billable row count. Rows skipped by `offset` are never returned and never charged.

**Filter naming.** Every filter below is accepted under two spellings: the camelCase name and its snake_case twin (`rentValueMin` / `rent_value_min`, `listedFromDate` / `listed_from_date`, `propertyType` / `property_type`, and so on). Supply either. If you supply both, the **camelCase value wins** and the snake_case value is discarded silently. An explicit `false` or `0` counts as a supplied value; only omitting a parameter falls through to its twin.

**Unrecognised parameters are rejected.** A query parameter this operation does not implement returns `400` with `error: "unknown_query_parameters"`, naming the offending parameters and — where one exists — the canonical parameter that replaces them. Nothing is queried and nothing is billed. Ignoring such a name, which is what happened before, turned a filtered-looking request into a billed, silently unfiltered result. Sold search shares this behaviour, with its own parameter set — `bedrooms` and `bathrooms` are real filters here and unknown there. A misspelling is never matched to a nearby parameter — the response lists `accepted_parameters` instead, so you can correct it yourself.

parameters.name: proximity
parameters.description:
Spatial relation between the search anchor and the rows returned (default: `any`). Values are case-sensitive.

- `any` — return listings within `radius` of the anchor.

- `sameStreet` — **`radius` is ignored.** Returns matching listings from anywhere on the anchor's street, however far from the anchor, with the other filters and `limit`/`offset` applying as usual. The street is matched on its canonical name, type and suffix within the anchor's suburb, so a same-named street in another suburb, a different street type (`King Street` vs `King Avenue`) and a longer name (`Main` vs `Main Ridge`) are all excluded. A listing whose address is not present in HtAG's address reference data cannot be confirmed to be on the street and is not returned. Listings still need coordinates to be returned, and `distance_km` can exceed `radius`. Requires `address` or `address_key` — a `lat`/`lon`-only anchor has no street to match and is rejected with `400`.

- `sameSuburb` — **`radius` is ignored.** Returns matching listings from anywhere in the anchor's suburb, however far from the anchor, with the other filters and `limit`/`offset` applying as usual. Listings still need coordinates to be returned. Requires `address` or `address_key` — a `lat`/`lon`-only anchor is rejected with `400`.

For each comparable the response includes a signed dollar adjustment for bed/bath/parking differences (the *structural leg*), a multiplicative size factor for land/floor-area differences (the *size leg*), a combined `adjusted_value`, and a confidence score (0–100).

H3MetricResponse.title: H3MetricResponse
H3MetricResponse.description: Envelope for H3 metric endpoints. Includes a top-level `viewport` object that map clients (Leaflet, Mapbox/MapLibre) can pass directly to `flyTo(center)` and `fitBounds(bbox)` without per-cell centroid lookups. Centroid is the unweighted mean of every returned cell's boundary vertices; bbox is the tight box around the same vertex set; `recommended_zoom` is a Web-Mercator heuristic assuming a 512px viewport with 10% padding around the bbox. Empty result set → `viewport: null`.

ViewportBbox.title: ViewportBbox
ViewportBbox.description: Tight bounding box around every returned cell's full boundary (not centroid — protects edge cells from being visually clipped on sparse-result maps). All four cardinals are WGS 84 degrees. AU-only data means `west < east` and `south < north` always.

ViewportMetadata.description: Top-level `viewport` on H3 metric responses. Wraps a center coordinate, tight bbox, and a `recommended_zoom` hint so clients can fit the result on a map without per-cell lookups.

nearest_roundabout_m.description: Metres to the nearest roundabout. Sentinel `200000` = no feature within range. Non-null.

roundabout_within_50m.description: Whether a roundabout is within 50 m of the address. Non-null.

roundabout_within_100m.description: Whether a roundabout is within 100 m of the address. Non-null.

SoldPropertyTypeSnake.name: property_type
SoldPropertyTypeSnake.description: snake_case alias of `propertyType`. Accepts the same canonical values, comma-separated or repeated. When both spellings are supplied, `propertyType` wins.

Radius.name: radius
Radius.description:
Search radius in **metres** (default 2000, max 5000). Values are metres, not kilometres — use `radius=5000` for a 5 km search, and `radius=2000` for 2 km. A value like `radius=5` means 5 metres and will almost always return zero results.

`radius` is applied only when `proximity` is `any` (the default). Both named modes ignore it: `proximity=sameSuburb` returns the whole suburb and `proximity=sameStreet` returns the whole street, each regardless of distance. The value is still range-checked even when it is ignored.

Address.name: address
Address.description: Query by a freeform Australian address.

MbCategory2021.name: mb_category_2021
MbCategory2021.description: Filter by Mesh Block category (defaults to Any)

PeriodEndMin.name: period_end_min
PeriodEndMin.description: Minimum period end date (ISO 8601 format) for trend filtering.

LegalParcelId.name: legal_parcel_id
LegalParcelId.description: Query by legal parcel ID (e.g., local council reference).

AreaIdRequired.name: area_id
AreaIdRequired.description: Array of area IDs (LGA or suburb identifiers). Required.

AddressKey.name: address_key
AddressKey.description: Query by a canonical address key.

PeriodEndMax.name: period_end_max
PeriodEndMax.description: Maximum period end date (ISO 8601 format) for trend filtering.

PropertyTypeRequired.name: property_type
PropertyTypeRequired.description: Property types to return. **Required** on this endpoint — it bills per returned row, so an unfiltered call would return both types and bill double.

Bedrooms.name: bedrooms
Bedrooms.description: Bedroom filter: All, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. 'All' returns aggregate data.

AddressKeys.name: address_keys
AddressKeys.description:
Up to 50 address key values.
**Only one of `address`, `address_keys`, or `legal_parcel_id` can be provided in a single request.**

AddressKeysRequired.name: address_keys
AddressKeysRequired.description: Up to 50 canonical address keys. CSV-encoded. **Required** — these endpoints have no other addressing mode; clients pre-resolve their address-key list via `/v1/reference/address-keys`.

H3Resolution.name: resolution
H3Resolution.description:
H3 resolution level (5–9). Lower = larger cells. Required — there is no server-side default.

When `strict_granularity` is true (the default), a fine geographic filter enforces a higher minimum: `loc_pid` rejects R5–R6 and `sa2_code` rejects R5. Pass `strict_granularity=false` to downgrade those rejections to a `granularity_warning`.

H3LocPid.name: loc_pid
H3LocPid.description: Filter by HTAG locality identifier (e.g. NSW3733).

H3LgaPid.name: lga_pid
H3LgaPid.description: Filter by HTAG LGA identifier (e.g. NSW200).

H3GccName.name: gcc_name
H3GccName.description: Filter by Greater Capital City Statistical Area name.

H3PropertyType.name: property_type
H3PropertyType.description: Filter by property type (house, unit, townhouse, land, rural).

H3StrictGranularity.name: strict_granularity
H3StrictGranularity.description: When true (the default), a geographic filter that is finer than the requested cell size is rejected with a `400 granularity_mismatch` instead of returning cells that spill outside the filter geography — `loc_pid` at R5–R6 and `sa2_code` at R5. Pass `false` to receive the cells anyway, with the reason surfaced in `granularity_warning`.
